title: The club that almost closed
body: Last term our school drama club had only four members. If nobody joined, the club would close. We felt helpless, because most students thought drama was only for people with a loud voice. Our teacher had one idea. "If you want new members, show them what you do," she said. So we put on a ten-minute play at lunchtime, right in the middle of the dining hall. Some students stopped eating. Some took out their phones. By Friday, eleven people came to ask about us. Now the club is full. We still lose our lines sometimes, and we still laugh at ourselves. But if a shy student comes to the door, we always say the same thing: come in and try one line. Because a club does not grow when you talk about it. It grows when people see it.

questions.q: Why did the drama club nearly close last term?
options: Because the teacher left the school.
Because the members were too busy.
Because it had too few members.
Because the dining hall was closed.
questions.explanation: 'Last term our school drama club had only four members. If nobody joined, the club would close.'

questions.q: What did the club do to get new members?
options: They performed a short play in the dining hall.
They put up posters in every classroom.
They asked the teacher to help them.
They made a video for the school website.
questions.explanation: 'So we put on a ten-minute play at lunchtime, right in the middle of the dining hall.'

questions.q: What does the writer want to tell us?
options: Drama is only for students with a loud voice.
A club needs a big room to grow.
Shy students should not join a drama club.
Showing what you do works better than talking about it.
questions.explanation: 'a club does not grow when you talk about it. It grows when people see it.'

title: My grandpa's radio
body: My grandpa keeps an old radio on the kitchen table. It is heavy and brown, and one button is missing. Every morning he turns it on while he makes tea. Last year I bought him a small speaker. "If you use this, you can hear a hundred stations," I said. He thanked me and put it on the shelf. The old radio stayed on the table. I did not understand, because the new one was clearly better. Then one evening he told me about my grandma. They listened to that radio together for thirty years. Since she passed, the morning music has been the one thing that still sounds like her. I stopped asking him to change. Now, when I visit, I make the tea and he turns on the radio. Some old things are not about sound at all.

questions.q: Why did the writer buy a speaker for grandpa?
options: Because the old radio was broken.
Because the writer thought it was better.
Because grandpa asked for one.
Because grandma liked new music.
questions.explanation: 'If you use this, you can hear a hundred stations,' 与 'because the new one was clearly better' 说明写作者认为新音箱更好。

questions.q: Why does grandpa keep using the old radio?
options: Because it is easy to move.
Because the speaker does not work.
Because it has more stations.
Because it reminds him of grandma.
questions.explanation: 'Since she passed, the morning music has been the one thing that still sounds like her.'

questions.q: How did the writer feel at the end?
options: He came to understand grandpa.
He was angry with grandpa.
He wanted to buy another speaker.
He was sorry he had visited.
questions.explanation: 'I stopped asking him to change. Now, when I visit, I make the tea and he turns on the radio.' 说明他理解了爷爷。

title: Two hours a week
body: Li Nan is fifteen. Every Sunday afternoon he spends two hours at the city library, but he does not go there to read. He goes to help small children choose books. He started last spring. Since his own reading was slow when he was seven, he knows how it feels to stand in front of a tall shelf and see nothing you can finish. "If a book is too hard, put it back," he tells them. "There is no prize for a thick book." Some parents were not happy at first, because they wanted their children to read long stories. Li Nan did not argue. He just kept coming. By June, twelve children were waiting for him at the door every Sunday. "If you enjoy the first ten pages, you will finish the book," he says. "That is the whole secret."

questions.q: What does Li Nan do at the library?
options: He reads long stories.
He works at the front desk.
He helps young children choose books.
He teaches parents how to read.
questions.explanation: 'He goes to help small children choose books.'

questions.q: Why can Li Nan understand the children so well?
options: Because he works with teachers.
Because his own reading was slow when he was young.
Because he reads a book every day.
Because his parents are librarians.
questions.explanation: 'Since his own reading was slow when he was seven, he knows how it feels…'

questions.q: What is Li Nan's advice to the children?
options: Start with a book you enjoy.
Always choose the thickest book.
Read for two hours every Sunday.
Ask your parents to choose for you.
questions.explanation: 'If a book is too hard, put it back.' 与 'If you enjoy the first ten pages, you will finish the book.'

title: The wall behind the school
body: The grey wall behind our school was ugly for years. Old posters hung on it, and nobody looked at them twice. In March, our art teacher asked a question: "If we cannot move the wall, can we change it?" Twenty of us said yes. We drew a river, a bridge and a line of young trees. Work was slow, because we could only paint after class. Some days it rained and we lost a whole afternoon. One boy wanted to stop. "Nobody will notice," he said. He was wrong. Since the wall was finished, three other classes have asked to paint the corner near the gate. Now people take photos there. If you walk past our school on a Friday, you will see a line of students with brushes, and a wall that keeps growing.

questions.q: What was the wall like before March?
options: It was covered with paintings.
It was grey with old posters on it.
It was hidden behind young trees.
It was used as a photo corner.
questions.explanation: 'The grey wall behind our school was ugly for years. Old posters hung on it…'

questions.q: Why did the work take a long time?
options: Because the wall was very high.
Because only two students helped.
Because the teacher was often away.
Because they could paint only after class and rain stopped them.
questions.explanation: 'Work was slow, because we could only paint after class. Some days it rained and we lost a whole afternoon.'

questions.q: What happened after the wall was finished?
options: The school painted it grey again.
The boy who wanted to stop left the school.
Other classes asked to paint another corner.
The teacher asked for new posters.
questions.explanation: 'Since the wall was finished, three other classes have asked to paint the corner near the gate.'
